D.153 communes des secteurs côtiers et sab: 153 communes in the coastal and sandy sectors (Atlantic seaboard), historically including the islands of Ré and Oléron. Light brandies that mature quickly.
D.22 communes autour de Segonzac. Sols arg: 22 communes around Segonzac. Chalky clay-limestone soils (Cretaceous). Brandies of great finesse, mainly floral, that mature slowly and need long ageing.
D.250 communes en couronne extérieure, sud: 250 communes in the outer ring, the south and the valleys. Sandy soils washed down from the Massif Central. Fruity brandies that mature quickly.
D.54 communes ceinturant la Grande Champag: 54 communes encircling the Grande Champagne to the south. Same chalky soils; a profile close to the Grande Champagne, peaking after shorter maturation. Part of “Fine Champagne”.
D.Aire sélective de 38 communes sur les co: A select area of 38 communes on the northern slopes; reds fuller than regional Beaujolais, plus rosés and whites (Chardonnay).
D.Altesse des coteaux de Frangy, en Haute-: Altesse from the slopes of Frangy, in Haute-Savoie, on the hillsides above the Usses.
D.Altesse du coteau de Montagnieu, sur la: Altesse from the Montagnieu slope, on the bend of the Rhône.
D.Altesse du cru de Marestel, sur les fort: Altesse from the Marestel cru, on the steep slopes of Jongieux facing the Lac du Bourget.
D.Altesse du cru de Monthoux, sur la commu: Altesse from the Monthoux cru, in the commune of Saint-Jean-de-Chevelu, on the side of the Mont du Chat.
D.Altesse du cru de Virieu-le-Grand, dans: Altesse from the Virieu-le-Grand cru, in the Valromey.
D.Amphithéâtre granitique en monopole à Vé: A granite amphitheatre held as a monopole at Vérin and Saint-Michel-sur-Rhône: broad, racy Viognier made for ageing — a historic curiosity of the valley.
D.Ancien vin favori d'Henri IV. Rouges fin: Once Henri IV's favourite wine. Fine, elegant, supple reds with silky tannins and fruity aromas turning spicy and gamey; dry whites, fresh and fruity with a touch of minerality.
D.Ancien îlot calcaire face à la mer, près: A former limestone island facing the sea near Narbonne; sun-drenched reds and Bourboulenc whites marked by sea spray.
D.Anjou-Villages Brissac : les rouges de c: Anjou-Villages Brissac: Cabernet reds from the Aubance slopes around Brissac, on slaty schist.
D.Appellation blanche du nord du Mâconnais: An all-white appellation in the north of the Mâconnais (Viré, Clessé, Laizé, Montbellet), recognised in 1999: rich, unctuous Chardonnay, sometimes with residual sugar.
D.Appellation d'assemblage de rouges issus: A blending appellation for reds from most villages of the Côte de Beaune (except Aloxe, Beaune, Pommard, Volnay): supple, fruity reds.
D.Appellation d'entrée de gamme couvrant t: The entry-level appellation covering all of Burgundy and the Beaujolais: Gamay/Pinot blends for reds, Chardonnay/Aligoté for whites.
D.Appellation de liaison groupant les extr: A linking appellation grouping the ends of the Côte de Nuits (Fixin, Brochon, Prissey, Comblanchien, Corgoloin): solid, affordable reds.
D.Appellation de plaine et de bas de cotea: An appellation of plain and lower slopes near Beaune: soft, fruity, easy-drinking reds.
D.Appellation exclusivement blanche (chard: An all-white (Chardonnay) appellation in the south of the Côte chalonnaise: dry, lively, mineral wines with floral (hawthorn, acacia) and citrus aromas, sometimes buttery and brioche-like after ageing.
D.Apéritif traditionnel jurassien, doux et: A traditional Jura aperitif, sweet and fortified, white, red or rosé; served chilled.
D.Arc de terroirs autour de Montpellier («: An arc of terroirs around Montpellier (“grès”); warm blended reds of Grenache, Syrah and Mourvèdre.
D.Assemblage traditionnel bourguignon de p: A traditional Burgundian blend of Pinot Noir (≥ 1/3) and Gamay, grown and vinified together: fruity, generous, easy-drinking reds and rosés.
D.Assemblage traditionnel de gamay et de p: A traditional blend of Gamay and Pinot Noir (at least one third) vinified together.
D.Au cœur du Var, sur les plateaux calcair: In the heart of the Var, on the limestone plateaus around Brignoles (350–500 m): fresher, livelier rosés and reds thanks to cool nights, in the wooded hinterland of Provence.
D.Au nord de la Drôme provençale (Tricasti: In the north of the Drôme provençale (Tricastin), renamed in 2010: fruity, peppery Grenache and Syrah reds, plus rosés and whites, in lavender and truffle country.
D.Au nord du Lot-et-Garonne, contre la Gir: In the north of Lot-et-Garonne, bordering the Gironde: dry and medium-sweet Sauvignon-Sémillon whites and Merlot-Cabernet reds, in the Bordeaux style.
D.Au nord-ouest de Carcassonne, seul vigno: North-west of Carcassonne, the only vineyard where Atlantic grapes (Cabernets, Merlot) meet Mediterranean ones (Grenache, Syrah).
D.Au pied de la colline de Corton, patrie: At the foot of the hill of Corton, home of the Corton (red) and Corton-Charlemagne (white) grands crus: reds that are firm and tannic when young.
D.Au pied des Alpilles autour des Baux-de-: At the foot of the Alpilles around Les Baux-de-Provence: warm reds of Grenache, Mourvèdre and Syrah, plus rosés and whites — an appellation largely farmed organically and biodynamically.
D.Au pied des falaises des calanques, entr: At the foot of the calanques cliffs, between Marseille and La Ciotat: mostly dry, fine, saline whites of Marsanne and Clairette — the classic partner for bouillabaisse — plus a few rosés and reds.
D.Au pied du Larzac autour de Saint-Saturn: At the foot of the Larzac around Saint-Saturnin; reds and rosés (including “vin d'une nuit”).
D.Au pied du Larzac, marqué par de fortes: At the foot of the Larzac, with wide day/night temperature swings; fresh, structured blended reds.
D.Au pied du Mont Ventoux : rouges frais e: At the foot of Mont Ventoux: fresh, fruity reds, lively rosés and taut whites from high slopes with cool nights — a lighter, more digestible Rhône.
D.Au sud de Cahors, sur les causses entre: South of Cahors, on the causses between the Lot and Tarn-et-Garonne: fruity, spicy reds and rosés of Cabernet Franc supported by Tannat and Merlot.
D.Autour de Chitry-le-Fort : chardonnay mi: Around Chitry-le-Fort: mineral Chardonnay and supple Pinot Noir, in the Chablis style.
D.Autour du Pic Saint-Loup et de l'Hortus,: Around the Pic Saint-Loup and the Hortus, north of Montpellier; Syrah leads fresh, fragrant reds, with a few rosés.
D.Autour du golfe de Porto-Vecchio, sur ar: Around the gulf of Porto-Vecchio, on decomposed granite cooled by the sea: fine whites and rosés, supple reds — the south-east of the island.
D.Aux confins du Berry et de la Marche : g: On the border of the Berry and the Marche: Gamay (and a little Pinot Noir) for reds, and the famous saignée “vin gris”.
D.Aux portes d'Orléans : blancs de chardon: At the gates of Orléans: Chardonnay (Auvernat Blanc) whites, reds and gris from Pinot Meunier and Pinot Noir.
D.Aux portes de Tonnerre : pinots noirs fi: At the gates of Tonnerre: fine, fragrant Pinot Noirs (red fruit, spice), sometimes made as rosé.
D.Aux portes du Marais poitevin, autour de: At the edge of the Marais poitevin, around Vix: Chenin, Chardonnay and Sauvignon whites, blended reds and rosés.
D.Berceau de l'effervescent (Blanquette de: The cradle of sparkling wine (Blanquette from Mauzac & the ancestral method); also oak-aged still whites of Chardonnay-Chenin-Mauzac and Merlot reds.
D.Berceau du vin effervescent (Blanquette: The cradle of sparkling wine (Blanquette & Mauzac ancestral method); also oak-aged still Chardonnay whites and Merlot reds.
D.Berceau historique du Crémant de Bourgog: The historic birthplace of Crémant de Bourgogne. Fine, floral, mineral whites (hawthorn, citrus, hazelnut); supple, fruity reds with mellow tannins.
D.Blanc d'altesse pure du Bugey, fin et ar: Pure Altesse white from the Bugey, fine and aromatic. Two dénominations: Montagnieu and Virieu-le-Grand.
D.Blanc de chasselas des coteaux dominant: Chasselas white from the slopes above Thonon, on the shore of Lake Geneva.
D.Blanc de chasselas du Chablais lémanique: Chasselas white from the Chablais on Lake Geneva, in the commune of Sciez.
D.Blanc de jacquère de la Combe de Savoie,: Jacquère white from the Combe de Savoie, around Montmélian.
Jacquère white from the Combe de Savoie, at Saint-Jeoire-Prieuré.
Jacquère white from the Combe de Savoie, in the commune of Cruet.
D.Blanc gras et aromatique (abricot, miel): A rich, aromatic white (apricot, honey) of Roussanne, known locally as Bergeron, on the steep slopes of Chignin and Montmélian.
D.Blanc léger et perlant de chasselas au b: A light, slightly sparkling Chasselas white on the shore of Lake Geneva, around Douvaine and Ballaison.
D.Blanc sec de chasselas, sur la grève lém: Dry Chasselas white from the Ripaille shore of Lake Geneva at Thonon-les-Bains.
D.Blanc sec et perlant de jacquère, léger: A dry, slightly sparkling Jacquère white, light and mineral, grown on the boulders of the great landslide of Mont Granier.
D.Blanc sec et tranquille de clairette, di: A dry, still Clairette white, the quiet companion of the Diois sparkling wines.
D.Blanc sec vif et salin autour de l'étang: A lively, saline dry white around the Étang de Thau; 100% Piquepoul, the partner of Bouzigues oysters.
D.Blanc tendre et floral de jacquère, embl: A soft, floral Jacquère white, emblem of the Avant-Pays savoyard, on the same scree as Les Abymes.
D.Blancs de chardonnay au sud de l'Yonne,: Chardonnay whites from the south of the Yonne, around Vézelay — straight, fresh, floral wines with chalky minerality. Promoted to village AOC in 2017.
D.Blancs de jacquère et rouges (gamay, mon: Jacquère whites and reds (Gamay, Mondeuse) from the Jongieux vineyard, west of the Lac du Bourget.
D.Blancs et fines bulles de gringet, cépag: Whites and sparkling wines from Gringet, a rare grape grown on the slopes of Ayze near Bonneville.
D.Blancs liquoreux, les plus riches de Mon: Sweet whites, the richest of Montravel, often botrytised — honey and candied fruit, on the heights facing the Dordogne.
D.Blancs moelleux (demi-doux) sur les cote: Medium-sweet whites on the northern slopes of the Montravel area — soft, fruity Sémillon and Muscadelle.
D.Cabernet franc de la rive droite de la L: Cabernet Franc from the right bank of the Loire, on gravel (supple) or tuffeau (for ageing), between Langeais and the Saumurois.
D.Cabernet franc sur les terrasses de grav: Cabernet Franc on the gravel terraces of the Loire; the most elegant and fruity of the Bourgueil reds.
D.Capitale des vins de Bourgogne, ceinturé: The capital of Burgundy wine, ringed with premiers crus on its slope: smooth, harmonious reds and a few whites, famous for the Hospices wine auction.
D.Chenin moelleux confidentiel des coteaux: A rare medium-sweet Chenin from the tuffeau slopes of the Saumurois.
D.Chenin moelleux des coteaux bordant la L: Medium-sweet Chenin from the slopes along the Loire downstream of Angers, between Savennières and Ingrandes.
D.Chenin moelleux à liquoreux des coteaux: Medium-sweet to sweet Chenin from the Aubance slopes, south of Angers.
D.Chenin sec et racé de la vallée du Loir,: A dry, racy Chenin from the Loir valley, on a single south-facing tuffeau slope at Lhomme and Ruillé.
D.Climat d'élite de Savennières : chenin s: Savennières's elite climat: powerful, mineral dry Chenin on the Roche aux Moines slope (enclave: the Coulée de Serrant).
D.Coteaux caillouteux du nord de l'Hérault: Stony slopes in the north of the Hérault; structured reds.
D.Coteaux de schiste au confluent du Lot e: Schist slopes at the confluence of the Lot and the Truyère: lively Chenin whites and light reds of Fer Servadou and Cabernet — a tiny vineyard.
D.Cru de la Drôme provençale : rouges frai: A cru of the Drôme provençale: fresh, peppery Grenache and Syrah reds from high slopes, with a milder climate than the plain.
D.Cru du cœur des Corbières (Boutenac et a: A cru at the heart of the Corbières (Boutenac and surroundings): powerful reds led by old-vine Carignan. Also called “Corbières-Boutenac”.
D.Cru liquoreux du Layon à Thouarcé : chen: A sweet Layon cru at Thouarcé: rich, racy botrytised Chenin on three schist slopes.
D.Dans les gorges du Tarn autour de Millau: In the Tarn gorges around Millau: Gamay and Syrah reds and rosés, Chenin and Mauzac whites — a high-altitude terraced vineyard.
D.De part et d'autre du Rhône, à Seyssel :: On both sides of the Rhône at Seyssel: fine Altesse whites and historic sparkling wines (Altesse, Molette, Chasselas).
D.Des deux rives de la Garonne autour de M: On both banks of the Garonne around Marmande: fruity, supple Cabernet-Merlot reds lifted by Abouriou, a local grape.
D.Deux terroirs (maritime autour de Fitou,: Two terroirs (maritime around Fitou, and upper Fitou in the Corbières); robust Carignan and Grenache reds. The oldest red AOC in the Languedoc.
D.Dénomination géographique (Montrecul / M: A geographical dénomination (Montrecul / Montre-Cul / En Montre-Cul) in the commune of Dijon: a tiny, historic urban vineyard.
D.Dénomination géographique créée en 2017: A geographical dénomination created in 2017 for red and white Bourgogne from the communes of the Côte de Nuits and Côte de Beaune only — the “premium” base of the pyramid.
D.Dénomination géographique sur la commune: A geographical dénomination in the commune of Chenôve, south of Dijon: reds and whites from a historically renowned lieu-dit.
A geographical dénomination in the commune of Ladoix-Serrigny: reds and whites at the foot of the hill of Corton.
D.Eau-de-vie de vin de la Charente, ~75 00: Wine brandy from the Charente, ~75,000 ha (Ugni Blanc ≈ 98%), across 734 communes. Six historic crus delimited by Coquand. “Fine Champagne” = a blend of Grande Champagne (≥ 50%) + Petite Champagne.
D.Effervescent de méthode traditionnelle a: Traditional-method sparkling wine around Limoux; a Chardonnay-Chenin base with Mauzac, aged on the lees ≥ 9 months.
D.Effervescent de méthode traditionnelle,: Traditional-method sparkling wine, white or rosé, made throughout Burgundy, including the Beaujolais.
D.En Balagne, sur les collines de granite: In the Balagne, on the granite hills around Calvi and L'Île-Rousse: Niellucciu and Sciaccarellu reds and rosés, Vermentinu whites, facing the sea.
D.En Sologne près de Blois : blancs d'asse: In the Sologne near Blois: blended Sauvignon-Chardonnay whites, Gamay and Pinot Noir reds.
D.En altitude : rouges tendres, délicats e: At altitude: soft, delicate, very fragrant reds, best drunk young.
D.En aval d'Agen, sur les deux rives de la: Downstream of Agen, on both banks of the Garonne: dark, robust reds of Tannat, Cabernets, Malbec and Merlot — heirs to the old “black wines”.
D.Entre Agen et la forêt landaise : rouges: Between Agen and the Landes forest: supple, fleshy Bordeaux-style reds (Merlot-Cabernets), a few rosés and whites — a pioneering cooperative cellar.
D.Entre Carcassonne et la Montagne Noire ;: Between Carcassonne and the Montagne Noire; generous Grenache and Syrah reds, a few whites and rosés.
D.Entre schistes au nord et argilo-calcair: Schist in the north, clay-limestone in the south; reds and rosés, a little white. Dénominations Berlou and Roquebrun.
D.Extrémité sud de la Côte de Beaune : rou: The southern end of the Côte de Beaune: sturdy, earthy reds and frank whites; a spa village with many premiers crus.
D.Face à Valence, blancs de marsanne et ro: Facing Valence, Marsanne and Roussanne whites — fine still wines and above all traditional-method sparklers, on granite and limestone at the foot of Crussol.
D.Fines bulles brut de clairette (méthode: Fine brut bubbles from Clairette (traditional method), more vinous and drier than Clairette de Die, on the same Diois slopes.
D.Grand blanc de Savoie : altesse pure, am: Savoie's great white: pure Altesse, broad and aromatic (dried fruit, honey), across the whole vineyard. Four dénominations: Frangy, Marestel, Monterminod, Monthoux.
D.Grand cru blanc au-dessus du Montrachet: A white grand cru above Le Montrachet: chiselled, taut, mineral Chardonnays.
D.Grand cru blanc majestueux de la colline: The majestic white grand cru of the hill of Corton: powerful, mineral Chardonnays for very long ageing.
D.Grand cru blanc partagé par Puligny et C: A white grand cru shared by Puligny and Chassagne: rich, powerful, opulent Chardonnays.
D.Grand cru de Gevrey au style parfumé et: A Gevrey grand cru with a fragrant, elegant style, on stony soils.
D.Grand cru de Gevrey ferme et structuré,: A firm, structured Gevrey grand cru, built for long ageing.
D.Grand cru de Gevrey pouvant se vendre en: A Gevrey grand cru that may be sold as Charmes-Chambertin; broad, generous reds.
D.Grand cru de Morey qui a donné son nom a: The Morey grand cru that gave the village its name: delicate, fragrant reds.
D.Grand cru de Vosne au style dentelé et p: A Vosne grand cru with a lacy, fragrant style, all finesse.
D.Grand cru en monopole à Morey, d'un seul: A monopole grand cru at Morey, in a single block for centuries: deep, silky reds.
D.Grand cru en monopole à Vosne : rouges s: A monopole grand cru at Vosne: sumptuous, spicy, intense reds, in the orbit of Romanée-Conti.
D.Grand cru en monopole à Vosne, ruban de: A monopole grand cru at Vosne, a ribbon of vines between Romanée-Conti and La Tâche.
D.Grand cru en quasi-monopole à Morey : ro: A near-monopole grand cru at Morey: spicy, floral, refined reds.
D.Grand cru historique jouxtant le Chamber: A historic grand cru next to Chambertin, just as noble; may be sold under the name Chambertin.
D.Grand cru mythique de Gevrey — « le vin: Gevrey's legendary grand cru — “the wine of kings”: Pinot Noir of majestic power and depth.
D.Grand cru opulent de Vosne : rouges rich: An opulent Vosne grand cru: rich, velvety, fleshy reds.
D.Grand cru plus restreint et régulier que: A smaller, more consistent grand cru than Echezeaux: deep, harmonious reds.
D.Grand cru voisin du Chambertin : rouges: A grand cru next to Chambertin: racy reds, slightly more airy and mineral.
D.Grand cru à cheval sur Chambolle et More: A grand cru straddling Chambolle and Morey: powerful, earthy reds for long ageing.
D.Grand cru étendu de Flagey près de Vosne: A large Flagey grand cru near Vosne: fragrant, fine reds, affordable for a grand cru.
D.Grand village de blancs (et de rouges) :: A great village for whites (and reds): rich, racy Chardonnays; co-owner of the Montrachet, Bâtard- and Criots-Bâtard-Montrachet grands crus.
D.Grand vin doux naturel du Roussillon (Au: The Roussillon's great vin doux naturel (Aude & Pyrénées-Orientales), made as ambré (white grapes, oxidative), tuilé and grenat (Grenache Noir); a long rancio tradition.
D.Grande commune vigneronne (avec Premeaux: A large wine commune (with Premeaux-Prissey), with no grand cru but many premiers crus: solid, spicy reds that age well.
D.L'appellation de base du Beaujolais, ici: The base appellation of the Beaujolais, here in its 11 communes in the south of Saône-et-Loire (granite slopes): supple, light, very fruity Gamay reds and rosés, plus a few Chardonnay whites.
D.L'appellation de base du Mâconnais, la p: The base appellation of the Mâconnais, the largest in the south of the département: lively, fruity Chardonnay whites, supple Gamay reds and rosés. May be followed by a commune name.
D.L'appellation de base du Roussillon, sur: The base appellation of the Roussillon, on the schist and clay-limestone hills around Perpignan: Mediterranean-blend reds and rosés, Grenache and Macabeu whites.
D.L'appellation entièrement dédiée au rosé: The appellation devoted entirely to rosé: full, deeply coloured rosés for ageing, blended (Grenache, Cinsault, Clairette…), on pebbles, sand and lauze stone — the historic rosé of the kings of France.
D.L'appellation la plus orientale et la pl: The easternmost and highest appellation of the Rhône, around Manosque on the Durance: lively reds, rosés and whites shaped by altitude and alpine influence.
D.L'appellation reine du vin effervescent,: The queen appellation of sparkling wine, across 617 communes in five départements.
D.L'appellation régionale : pinot noir en: The regional appellation: Pinot Noir for reds, Chardonnay for whites, across all of Burgundy.
D.L'appellation régionale angevine : rouge: Anjou's regional appellation: Cabernet Franc reds and dry Chenin whites, on the schist of “black Anjou” and the tuffeau of “white Anjou”.
D.L'appellation régionale du Béarn : rosés: The regional appellation of the Béarn: rosés (the speciality) and reds of Tannat and Cabernets, Manseng and Raffiat whites — around Salies-de-Béarn, Bellocq and the Vic-Bilh.
D.L'appellation régionale la plus large de: Burgundy's widest regional appellation (from Chablis to the Beaujolais): supple, fruity reds of Gamay and/or Pinot Noir, versatile whites. “Clairet”, “primeur” / “nouveau” mentions allowed.
D.L'appellation régionale phare de la Bour: Burgundy's flagship regional appellation: supple, fruity Pinot Noir reds (cherry, red fruit), fresh, floral Chardonnay whites, plus rosés and “clairet”. The base of the Burgundy pyramid.
D.L'appellation régionale tourangelle : sa: Touraine's regional appellation: lively Sauvignon for whites, Gamay and Côt (Malbec) for reds. Five dénominations — Amboise, Azay-le-Rideau, Chenonceaux, Mesland, Oisly.
D.L'appellation régionale, du Gard à l'Aud: The regional appellation from the Gard to the Aude, along the Gulf of Lion: Mediterranean blends in red, rosé and white, with many geographical dénominations (terroirs).
D.L'appellation régionale-mère de la Bourg: Burgundy's parent regional appellation: Pinot Noir for reds, Chardonnay for whites; in the Beaujolais crus, reds may come from Gamay.
D.L'appellation-socle de Savoie : blancs d: Savoie's base appellation: Jacquère and Altesse whites, Mondeuse, Gamay and Pinot reds, rosés and sparkling wines, across the Avant-Pays, the Combe de Savoie and the lake shores.
D.L'appellation-socle du vignoble nantais: The base appellation of the Nantes vineyard: Melon de Bourgogne (Muscadet) made dry, light and lively, along the Loire, the Sèvre and the Lac de Grand-Lieu.
D.L'autre blanc de Pouilly, issu du chasse: Pouilly's other white, from the historic Chasselas: a light, soft, fruity wine to drink young.
D.L'autre grand blanc sec du Mâconnais, en: The Mâconnais's other great dry white, surrounding Pouilly-Fuissé across seven communes: fine, fresh, fruity Chardonnay with floral and citrus notes.
D.L'expression la plus dentelée de la Côte: The most lace-like expression of the Côte de Nuits: airy, fragrant, silky reds, crowned by the Musigny and Bonnes-Mares grands crus.
D.L'insolite blanc du romorantin, cépage r: The unusual white from Romorantin, a rare grape planted by François I, on the sands of the Sologne around Cour-Cheverny.
D.L'une des plus anciennes AOC de France :: One of France's oldest AOCs: Sauvignon on the sand and gravel terraces of the Cher, at Quincy and Brinay; a lively, floral white.
D.L'unique blanc régional de Bourgogne iss: Burgundy's only regional white made from Aligoté: lively, floral and lemony — the soul of the Burgundian kir (with Dijon crème de cassis). Made throughout Burgundy; shown here, its communes in the Yonne.
D.LA spécialité du Bugey : rosé pétillant: THE Bugey speciality: a soft, fruity sparkling rosé (strawberry, raspberry) made by the ancestral method from Gamay and Poulsard, around Cerdon.
D.La borne méridionale de la Côte de Beaun: The southern end of the Côte de Beaune, straddling three communes of Saône-et-Loire: solid, rustic reds, rich in premiers crus.
D.La bulle emblématique du Diois : mousseu: The emblematic bubbles of the Diois: a sweet, aromatic sparkling wine from Muscat à petits grains made by the ancestral method, in the upper Drôme valley. The area also produces Crémant de Die (Clairette, traditional method) and Coteaux de Die (still Clairette).
D.La mythique colline dominant Tain-l'Herm: The legendary hill above Tain-l'Hermitage (granite, loess, pebbles): monumental Syrahs for ageing and great Marsanne whites — one of the historic peaks of Syrah.
D.La plus large appellation de vin doux na: The Roussillon's widest vin doux naturel appellation, encompassing the Rivesaltes area; little produced today.
D.La plus vaste appellation de Provence et: Provence's largest appellation and the world centre of rosé: pale, dry, fruity rosés (Grenache, Cinsault, Tibouren), alongside reds and Rolle whites, from the Maures massif to the foot of the Sainte-Victoire.
D.La plus vaste appellation de la Côte cha: The largest appellation of the Côte chalonnaise, mainly red: garnet colour, red-fruit and spice aromas, firm tannins and good ageing potential; rich, floral, vinous whites.
D.La plus vaste appellation du Rhône nord,: The largest appellation of the northern Rhône, around the hill of Hermitage: fruity, generous Syrahs (pebbles in the south, granite in the north) and supple whites — the sector's great playground.
D.La plus vaste des appellations communale: The largest of the Jura's village appellations, around the wine town of Arbois; the home ground of Ploussard and Trousseau.
D.La plus vaste des grandes communes de la: The largest of the great communes of the Côte de Nuits, home to nine grands crus including Chambertin — powerful, fleshy reds built for ageing.
D.La porte nord de la Côte de Nuits et la: The northern gateway to the Côte de Nuits and Burgundy's only village appellation for all three colours — known for its Pinot Noir rosés, firm reds and improving whites.
D.La référence mondiale du sauvignon : bla: The world benchmark for Sauvignon: lively, mineral whites on “terres blanches” (marl), caillottes and flint, around the hill of Sancerre; Pinot Noir reds and rosés.
D.Le blanc de la même aire que Madiran : m: The white from the same area as Madiran: Mansengs and Arrufiac, made lively and dry or rich and sweet (late harvest), aromatic and nervy.
D.Le blanc régional de Bourgogne issu du c: Burgundy's regional white made from Aligoté: lively and nervy, with green apple, citrus and a frank acidity. The traditional base of kir.
D.Le blanc vif et acidulé du folle blanche: The lively, tangy white from Folle Blanche (Gros Plant), the partner of oysters and seafood from the Atlantic coast, across the whole Nantes area.
D.Le blanc vif et frais de Bourgogne, issu: Burgundy's lively, fresh white, made exclusively from Aligoté B.
D.Le chenin de la rive droite de la Loire: Chenin from the right bank of the Loire east of Tours, on tuffeau: from dry to sweet, plus great traditional-method sparkling wines.
D.Le cru le plus septentrional : rouges te: The northernmost cru: soft, easy-drinking reds with red-fruit and spice aromas.
D.Le cru le plus vaste (249 communes), env: The largest cru (249 communes), surrounding the Champagnes and the Borderies. Red, stony clay-limestone “groies” (Jurassic). Round, supple brandies with a fruity bouquet of pressed grapes; quick to mature.
D.Le cœur du vignoble, sur les deux rives: The heart of the vineyard, on both banks of the Serein. Dry, taut, mineral Chardonnay — citrus, gunflint, white flowers; the salty finish typical of the Kimmeridgian.
D.Le cœur historique et qualitatif du Musc: The historic, top-quality heart of Muscadet, between the Sèvre nantaise and the Maine (Clisson, Vallet, Le Pallet): Melon on gabbro and mica-schist, often “sur lie”. Three village crus — Clisson, Gorges, Le Pallet.
D.Le cœur qualitatif des Côtes du Rhône :: The quality heart of the Côtes du Rhône: more concentrated blended reds (Grenache ≥ 50%) from selected terroirs, plus rosés and whites. Twenty communes or groups of communes may add their name (geographical dénominations).
D.Le grand blanc de viognier, sur des terr: The great Viognier white, on granite terraces (arzelle) above the Rhône: rich, opulent, apricot, white peach and violet. Dry, sometimes medium-sweet.
D.Le grand blanc du Béarn, sur les coteaux: The Béarn's great white, on the steep slopes south of Pau: lively, exuberant Mansengs — taut dry wines or golden late-harvest sweet wines (candied citrus, spice, honey).
D.Le grand chenin sec de l'Anjou, sur schi: Anjou's great dry Chenin, on schist and volcanic rhyolite on the north bank of the Loire; taut, mineral wines for long ageing.
D.Le grand cru du Rhône sud, sur les galet: The great cru of the southern Rhône, on the rolled pebbles and safres between Orange and Avignon: powerful, spicy, warm reds led by Grenache (up to 13 grapes), and rare rich whites. The cradle of the AOC system.
D.Le grand cru le plus célèbre du monde, e: The most famous grand cru in the world, a monopole at Vosne: Pinot Noir of unique complexity and length.
D.Le grand cru le plus racé de Chambolle :: Chambolle's most refined grand cru: Pinot Noir of incomparable airy elegance (plus a rare white Musigny).
D.Le grand effervescent de méthode traditi: The great traditional-method sparkling wine of the whole Loire Valley (Chenin, Chardonnay, Cabernet…), made mainly in the Saumurois.
D.Le grand liquoreux du Bergeracois, face: The great sweet wine of the Bergeracois, facing Bergerac on the left bank: botrytised Sémillon, deep gold, honey, candied apricot and dried fruit.
D.Le grand rouge du Saumurois : cabernet f: The Saumurois's great red: Cabernet Franc on tuffeau, fruity and supple to structured, across eight communes around Champigny.
D.Le grand vin liquoreux de l'Anjou : chen: Anjou's great sweet wine: botrytised Chenin on the schist slopes of the Layon. Seven villages may add their name; Chaume is a premier cru.
D.Le joyau de la Côte de Nuits : rouges d': The jewel of the Côte de Nuits: reds of legendary texture and refinement, home of Romanée-Conti and six other grands crus.
D.Le long de la Loire de Gien à Cosne : bl: Along the Loire from Gien to Cosne: Sauvignon whites, blended Gamay-Pinot Noir reds and rosés.
D.Le mousseux de méthode traditionnelle de: Burgundy's traditional-method sparkling wine, white or rosé, aged at least 9 months on the lees. Led by Chardonnay and Pinot Noir: fine bubbles, freshness and brioche notes.
D.Le niveau supérieur du Beaujolais généri: The step above generic Beaujolais, on the same slopes in the south of the département: more concentrated, structured Gamay, generous reds, plus rosés and Chardonnay whites.
D.Le pendant de Vouvray sur la rive gauche: Vouvray's counterpart on the left bank, between the Cher and the Loire: dry, off-dry, medium-sweet and sparkling Chenin.
D.Le pendant tout en finesse de Pommard :: Pommard's finely-drawn counterpart: delicate, floral, silky reds, among the most elegant of the Côte de Beaune.
D.Le plus grand blanc sec du monde, à chev: The greatest dry white in the world, straddling Puligny and Chassagne: Chardonnay of unrivalled richness and depth.
D.Le plus grand nom des blancs de la Côte: The greatest name among Côte de Beaune whites: rich, buttery, opulent Chardonnays, from a large vineyard rich in premiers crus.
D.Le plus haut des muscats languedociens,: The highest of the Languedoc Muscats, on a causse at ~200 m north of the Minervois; a fine, floral vin doux naturel.
D.Le plus jeune cru (1988) : rouges fruité: The youngest cru (1988): fruity, supple reds on granitic sand.
D.Le plus petit cru : 6 communes au nord-o: The smallest cru: 6 communes north-west of Cognac. Flinty clay-silica soils. Round, soft, fragrant brandies with a characteristic violet scent; short maturation.
D.Le plus petit cru : rouges charpentés et: The smallest cru: sturdy, floral reds (peony, rose), around Chénas.
D.Le plus petit grand cru (et la plus peti: The smallest grand cru (and smallest AOC) in France, a monopole at Vosne, next to Romanée-Conti.
D.Le plus petit grand cru de la Côte de Be: The smallest grand cru of the Côte de Beaune, at Chassagne: racy, rare Chardonnay.
D.Le plus prestigieux des blancs du Mâconn: The most prestigious Mâconnais white, on the limestone slopes below the rocks of Solutré and Vergisson: broad, rich, mineral Chardonnay. 22 climats classified as premier cru since 2020.
D.Le plus septentrional des dix crus du Be: The northernmost of the ten Beaujolais crus — and the only one in Saône-et-Loire (commune of Saint-Amour-Bellevue). Soft, fleshy Gamay reds with red fruit, peony and spice.
D.Le plus vaste des crus : rouges souples: The largest cru: supple, fruity reds (red fruit), in the south of the vineyard.
D.Le plus vaste des grands crus de Gevrey: The largest of the Gevrey grands crus (with Mazoyères): fleshy, round, charming reds.
D.Le plus vaste grand cru de Morey : rouge: The largest grand cru in Morey: powerful, structured reds for long ageing.
D.Le plus vaste terroir des Fiefs, autour: The largest terroir of the Fiefs, around Mareuil-sur-Lay: reds and rosés of Négrette, Pinot Noir, Cabernet Franc and Gamay, a few Chenin whites.
D.Le plus vaste vignoble du Languedoc, sur: The largest vineyard in the Languedoc, on the hills between Carcassonne, Narbonne and the Corbières; age-worthy reds led by Carignan, Grenache and Syrah.
D.Le rosé demi-sec emblématique de l'Anjou: Anjou's emblematic off-dry rosé: Cabernet Franc and Cabernet Sauvignon, soft and fruity.
D.Le rouge le plus structuré du Bergeracoi: The most structured red of the Bergeracois, north-east of the town: a tannic, sturdy Bordeaux blend that ages well.
D.Le rouge le plus viril de la Côte de Bea: The most powerful red of the Côte de Beaune: dark colour, strong, firm tannins and great ageing potential; Pinot Noir only.
D.Le rouge phare de Touraine : cabernet fr: Touraine's flagship red: Cabernet Franc on gravel and tuffeau, from fruity and generous to age-worthy; a few Chenin whites.
D.Le seul Grand Cru de la Loire : chenin l: The Loire's only Grand Cru: an exceptional sweet Chenin, from a schist amphitheatre above the Layon at Rochefort-sur-Loire.
D.Le seul grand cru rouge de la Côte de Be: The only red grand cru of the Côte de Beaune (plus a little white), on the hill of Corton: firm reds for long ageing.
D.Le seul vignoble du Pays basque nord, en: The only vineyard in the northern Basque Country, terraced at the foot of the Pyrenees: deeply coloured, sturdy Tannat and Cabernet reds and rosés, and rare Courbu and Manseng whites.
D.Le socle du Bergeracois : rouges souples: The base of the Bergeracois: supple Merlot and Cabernet reds, dry Sémillon and Sauvignon whites, lively rosés, on the slopes of both banks of the Dordogne.
D.Le socle régional couvrant toute l'île :: The regional base covering the whole island: Niellucciu, Sciaccarellu and Grenache reds and rosés, Vermentinu whites, mostly on the eastern plain (Aléria). Five terroirs may add their name.
D.Le socle régional de toute la vallée : d: The regional base for the whole valley: in the north, a few slope and plain communes for Syrah and Grenache reds, rosés and whites — the entry level of the Côtes du Rhône.
D.Le socle régional qui irrigue toute la v: The regional base that runs through the whole valley: generous Grenache and Syrah reds, rosés and whites, on the vast terraces and plains of both banks of the southern Rhône.
D.Le sommet de Banyuls : ≥ 75 % grenache n: The top of Banyuls: ≥ 75% Grenache Noir and long oxidative ageing (≥ 30 months in cask); deep rancio.
D.Le vignoble de la Limagne autour de Cler: The Limagne vineyard around Clermont-Ferrand, on volcanic and limestone slopes: Gamay and Pinot Noir for reds, Chardonnay for whites. Five crus — Boudes, Chanturgue, Châteaugay, Corent, Madargues.
D.Le vignoble le plus septentrional de Lor: Lorraine's northernmost vineyard, with a Germanic palette. Lively, floral whites of Auxerrois, Pinot Blanc and Pinot Gris, with Riesling, Gewurztraminer and Müller-Thurgau; light reds and “gris” of Pinot Noir and Gamay. Three sectors along the Moselle and the Seille.
D.Le « roi du vin jaune » : cru historique: The “king of vin jaune”: a historic cru perched above its blind valley, reserved for Savagnin alone — no red, no rosé, no topped-up white.
D.Le « vin noir » du Lot : malbec profond: The “black wine” of the Lot: deep, tannic Malbec on the Lot terraces and the Quercy causses — black fruit, liquorice, violet, long ageing.
D.Les blancs de chardonnay du Mâconnais (m: Mâconnais Chardonnay whites (“Villages” mention or a commune name, e.g. Mâcon-Lugny, Mâcon-Chardonnay): more structure and typicity than generic Mâcon.
D.Les coteaux autour d'Auxerre (Augy, Vaux: The slopes around Auxerre (Augy, Vaux, Saint-Bris) — fruity Pinot Noir reds and lively Chardonnay whites.
D.Les vins secs des mêmes terrasses de sch: The dry wines from the same schist terraces as Banyuls (Côte Vermeille): powerful Grenache and Mourvèdre reds, sea-influenced rosés and whites.
D.Les vins tranquilles de la même aire que: The still wines from the same area as Champagne (Bouzy, Aÿ, Cumières, Les Riceys…).
D.Longue guirlande de coteaux granitiques: A long garland of granite slopes on the right bank, from Chavanay to Guilherand: fragrant, supple Syrahs, Marsanne and Roussanne whites — the approachable face of the northern Rhône.
D.L’appellation-socle du Jura, étirée sur: The Jura's base appellation, stretching across the whole Revermont; every Jura style, from light Ploussard to vin jaune.
D.L’effervescent du Jura, produit sur tout: The Jura's sparkling wine, made across the whole regional area; Chardonnay leads the white cuvées.
D.Melon de Bourgogne des coteaux de la Loi: Melon de Bourgogne from the Loire slopes upstream of Nantes, around Ancenis and Saint-Herblon, on schist and gneiss.
D.Melon des terroirs sableux et de gneiss: Melon from the sandy and gneiss terroirs around the Lac de Grand-Lieu, south-west of Nantes; round, saline wines.
D.Mention réservée aux blancs secs des mei: A mention reserved for dry whites from the best slopes on the right bank of the Tarn, around Cahuzac and Cordes — more concentrated Mauzac and Loin de l'Œil.
D.Minuscule appellation dominée par le Clo: A tiny appellation overlooked by the Clos de Vougeot; velvety reds and a rare white from the land at the foot of the famous Cistercian clos.
D.Minuscule appellation sur les collines d: A tiny appellation on the hills of Nice (Saint-Roman-de-Bellet): local Braquet and Folle Noire grapes for reds and rosés, Rolle for racy whites — a rare urban vineyard on pebble terraces.
D.Minuscule grand cru de Gevrey aux arômes: A tiny Gevrey grand cru with cherry (griotte) aromas, all finesse.
D.Minuscule terroir de blancs ciselés, rép: A tiny terroir of finely-chiselled whites, known for its vins jaunes and vins de paille, on marl full of “star” fossils.
D.Muscat doux naturel emblématique, autour: The emblematic Muscat vin doux naturel, around Frontignan; a sweet white with a fresh-grape nose. Also “Frontignan” / “Vin de Frontignan”.
D.Muscat doux naturel voisin de Frontignan: A Muscat vin doux naturel next to Frontignan, at the foot of the Gardiole.
D.Même aire que Bergerac mais rendements p: The same area as Bergerac but with lower yields and higher alcohol: more concentrated age-worthy reds and richer medium-sweet or dry whites.
D.Même aire que Madiran : mansengs et arru: The same area as Madiran: Mansengs and Arrufiac made as lively dry whites or rich sweet wines (late harvest), aromatic and nervy.
D.Petit cru d'altesse au-dessus de Saint-A: A small Altesse cru above Saint-Alban-Leysse, near Chambéry.
D.Petit cru de liquoreux à l'ouest de Monb: A small sweet-wine cru west of Monbazillac: raisined/botrytised Sémillon and Muscadelle, sweet and unctuous, across four communes.
D.Petit cru réputé (Cheignieu-la-Balme, Pu: A small, renowned cru (Cheignieu-la-Balme, Pugieu): Chardonnay whites and Pinot Noir reds, on a well-exposed slope dear to Brillat-Savarin.
D.Petit grand cru blanc de Puligny, dans l: A small white grand cru in Puligny, in the wake of Bâtard: fine, elegant Chardonnays.
D.Petit grand cru de Gevrey sur sols pierr: A small Gevrey grand cru on stony soils: fine, chiselled reds for ageing.
D.Petit terroir au nord-est de Montpellier: A small terroir north-east of Montpellier; blended reds.
D.Petit terroir près de Fontenay-le-Comte: A small terroir near Fontenay-le-Comte: blended reds and rosés and Chenin whites, on limestone slopes.
D.Petit vignoble corrézien autour de Branc: A small Corrèze vineyard around Branceilles, Meyssac and Turenne, on the edge of the Périgord: Cabernet Franc reds and Chenin whites, on the sandstone terraces of the Bas-Limousin.
D.Petit vignoble d'altitude autour de Chât: A small high-altitude vineyard around Châtillon-en-Diois, east of Die: Gamay reds (with Pinot and Syrah) and Aligoté and Chardonnay whites, in an alpine cirque.
D.Petit vignoble de Tarn-et-Garonne et Hau: A small vineyard in Tarn-et-Garonne and Haute-Garonne: deeply coloured, spicy Syrah and Tannat reds and rosés, around Saint-Sardos.
D.Petit vignoble de clairette dans la Cost: A small Clairette vineyard in the Costière du Gard, near Bellegarde: dry white.
D.Petit vignoble de la vallée du Loir (à n: A small vineyard in the Loir valley (not to be confused with the Loire): Chenin for whites, Pineau d'Aunis and Gamay for reds/rosés.
D.Petit village robuste de la Côte de Nuit: A small, robust Côte de Nuits village: full-bodied, deeply coloured reds that age well, in the line of neighbouring Gevrey, plus a few whites.
D.Petite appellation confidentielle (commu: A small, little-known appellation (commune of Vinzelles): ripe, round, mineral Chardonnay, in the wake of Pouilly-Fuissé.
D.Petite appellation de chardonnay voisine: A small Chardonnay appellation next to Pouilly-Fuissé (hamlet of Loché, commune of Mâcon): supple, floral, rich whites. May also be sold as Pouilly-Vinzelles.
D.Petite appellation rouge nichée entre Me: A small red appellation tucked between Meursault and Puligny (its whites take the names of those villages): firm, racy high-altitude reds.
D.Petite appellation sur les hauteurs de B: A small appellation on the heights above Beaune (not to be confused with “Côte de Beaune-Villages”): reds and whites from the slopes.
D.Premier cru du Minervois (La Livinière e: The premier cru of the Minervois (La Livinière and neighbouring communes), on the terraces at the foot of the Montagne Noire: concentrated reds. Called “Minervois-la-Livinière”.
D.Promu cru en 2016 : rouges élégants et d: Promoted to cru in 2016: elegant, digestible reds (Grenache, Mourvèdre, Syrah) and Clairette whites on the terraces and combes of Cairanne, between the Aigues and the Ouvèze.
D.Rare blanc moelleux (demi-doux) sur les: A rare medium-sweet white on the slopes north of Bergerac, around Prigonrieux and Lembras — soft, floral, honeyed Sémillon.
D.Rare vin effervescent rouge de méthode t: A rare traditional-method red sparkling wine, a historic Burgundy speciality.
D.Rareté bourguignonne : le seul mousseux: A Burgundian rarity: Burgundy's only red sparkling wine, made by the traditional method from Gamay and Pinot Noir. Sparkling, fruity and light.
D.Rive droite face à Châteauneuf : la seul: On the right bank facing Châteauneuf: the only Rhône appellation to shine in all three colours — structured reds, rosés and whites — on pebbles and sand, next to Tavel.
D.Robe or pâle légèrement vert d'eau ; nez: Pale gold with a light green tint; acacia, white flowers and hazelnut on the nose, often mineral (flint) and lemony. Round and persistent on the palate, with mouth-watering liveliness — Burgundy's only village devoted to Aligoté.
D.Rosé sec régional d'Anjou, de Saumur et: Regional dry rosé from Anjou, Saumur and Touraine: a blend based on Cabernet, Gamay and Grolleau.
D.Rosé tendre et léger d'Anjou, à base de: A soft, light rosé from Anjou, made from Grolleau, Gamay and Cabernet.
D.Rouge d'exception sur les terrasses vert: An exceptional red from the dizzying terraces on the right bank at Ampuis (schistous Côte Brune, granitic Côte Blonde): deep, floral, smoky Syrah, sometimes softened with a touch of Viognier.
D.Rouge de mondeuse pure, coloré, épicé (p: A pure Mondeuse red, deeply coloured, spicy (pepper, violet) and tannic, on the slopes of Arbin.
D.Rouge de mondeuse pure, épicé et charpen: A pure Mondeuse red, spicy and sturdy, on the slopes of Saint-Jean-de-la-Porte.
D.Rouge exclusif de cabernet franc sur la: An all-Cabernet Franc red from the left bank of the Loire, around Cléry-Saint-André.
D.Rouge noir, dense et solaire de pure syr: An inky, dense, sun-drenched red of pure Syrah, from the curved granite slopes of the single commune of Cornas — “burnt earth” in Celtic, one of the great age-worthy wines of the Rhône.
D.Rouges charpentés de grenache au pied de: Sturdy Grenache reds at the foot of the Dentelles de Montmirail — spice, garrigue and black fruit; generous rosés and, since 2023, a few Clairette whites.
D.Rouges corsés et épicés, aptes à la gard: Full-bodied, spicy reds for ageing, on the border between the Rhône and Saône-et-Loire.
D.Rouges de gamay souples et blancs de jac: Supple Gamay reds and Jacquère whites, on the Chautagne slopes north of the Lac du Bourget.
D.Rouges de pinot noir, parfois relevés d': Pinot Noir reds, sometimes lifted with a touch of César — red and black fruit, spice, fine and firm structure. One of the Yonne's rare red villages.
D.Rouges et rosés de tannat et cabernets,: Tannat and Cabernet reds and rosés, Manseng whites — the regional appellation of the Béarn, a few of whose communes spill over into the Gers.
D.Rouges gouleyants et fruités issus du ga: Easy-drinking, fruity Gamay reds; lively rosés and rarer Chardonnay whites.
D.Rouges puissants qui « morgonnent » : no: Powerful reds that “morgonner”: cherry and kirsch notes, good ageing (Côte du Py).
D.Rouges secs, riches et solaires de grena: Rich, sun-drenched dry Grenache reds on the clay-limestone slopes of Rasteau, promoted to cru in 2010 — on the same land as the historic vin doux naturel.
D.Rouges seuls, sur les terres rouges (tri: Reds only, on the red soils (Triassic) and sandstone south of the Dentelles: deep Grenache and Syrah. Distinct from the famous Muscat de Beaumes-de-Venise (white VDN).
D.Rouges souples et fruités à dominante me: Supple, fruity Merlot-led reds, aromatic and fresh dry whites, lively and generous rosés and clairets.
D.Réservée aux blancs, sur les coteaux kim: Reserved for whites, on the Kimmeridgian slopes of the Tonnerrois — Tonnerre, Épineuil and neighbouring communes. Lively, mineral Chardonnay in the fresh style of northern Burgundy.
D.Réservée aux rouges, sur la moitié nord: Reserved for reds, in the northern half (Agly valley); concentrated blends. Five village dénominations: Caramany, Latour-de-France, Lesquerde, Tautavel and Les Aspres.
D.Sauvignon de la rive droite de la Loire,: Sauvignon from the right bank of the Loire, facing Sancerre, on flint (“pierre à fusil”) and Kimmeridgian marl; a racy white with smoky notes.
D.Sauvignon vif et aromatique — buis, agru: Lively, aromatic Sauvignon — boxwood, citrus, blackcurrant bud, mineral notes. Burgundy's odd one out, on the slopes of Saint-Bris-le-Vineux.
D.Sommet mondial du chardonnay : blancs ci: The world summit of Chardonnay: finely-chiselled, floral, mineral whites, sharing the Montrachet and Bâtard-Montrachet grands crus with Chassagne.
D.Sur le massif de la Malepère, à l'ouest: On the Malepère massif, west of Carcassonne: Atlantic influence, reds based on Merlot and Cabernet Franc.
D.Sur les arènes granitiques du golfe d'Aj: On the decomposed granite of the Gulf of Ajaccio and the Gravona valley: fine, peppery reds led by the local Sciaccarellu, delicate rosés and Vermentinu whites.
D.Sur les contreforts des monts du Forez,: On the foothills of the Monts du Forez, south of Montbrison: Gamay only, as fruity reds and lively rosés.
D.Sur les coteaux argilo-calcaires du Nebb: On the clay-limestone slopes of the Nebbio, at the foot of Cap Corse (Gulf of Saint-Florent): great Niellucciu reds (a cousin of Sangiovese), rosés and 100% Vermentinu whites — the birthplace of Corsican AOCs (1968).
D.Sur les coteaux argilo-calcaires à cheva: On clay-limestone slopes straddling the Gers, Hautes-Pyrénées and Béarn: a powerful, tannic Tannat red, dark and sturdy, that softens with age.
D.Sur les coteaux de l'Adour au sud-ouest: On the Adour slopes in the south-west of the Gers: Tannat and Pinenc reds, dry Arrufiac and Manseng whites, rosés — the vineyard of the Producteurs Plaimont.
D.Sur les coteaux de schiste de la vallée: On the schist slopes of the Vézère valley near Brive: lively Chenin whites and Cabernet Franc reds — the white dénomination of the Corrèze AOC.
D.Sur les coteaux du Cher et de l'Arnon :: On the slopes of the Cher and the Arnon: Sauvignon for whites, Pinot Noir for reds, and a renowned Pinot Gris rosé.
D.Sur les côtes calcaires à l'ouest de Tou: On the limestone slopes west of Toul, in a bend of the Moselle. Its emblem: vin gris, a pale, lively rosé of Gamay and Pinot Noir. Also fine red Pinot Noirs and rare whites of Auxerrois and Aubin, a local grape.
D.Sur les deux rives du Tarn autour d'Albi: On both banks of the Tarn around Albi: a unique palette — dry, sweet and perlé whites of Mauzac and Loin de l'Œil, Duras and Braucol reds, ancestral-method sparkling wines.
D.Sur les fortes pentes de la boucle du Rh: On the steep slopes of the bend of the Rhône (Briord, Montagnieu, Seillonnaz): lively white sparkling and semi-sparkling wines and Mondeuse reds.
D.Sur les pentes de schiste bleu du mont B: On the blue-schist slopes of Mont Brouilly: structured reds with black-fruit and floral notes.
D.Sur les pentes granitiques dominant Roan: On the granite slopes above Roanne and the Loire: Gamay (called “Saint-Romain”) as generous reds and rosés.
D.Sur les plateaux calcaires (Portlandien): On the limestone (Portlandian) plateaus above the Chablis slopes. A lively, fresh, lighter wine, with white fruit and citrus — to drink young.
D.Sur les reliefs du Luberon, au sud de la: On the Luberon hills, south of the Durance: fresh whites and rosés play a big part (high-altitude climate), alongside supple Grenache and Syrah reds.
D.Sur les restanques en amphithéâtre autou: On the amphitheatre of terraces (restanques) around the bay of Bandol: powerful, tannic Mourvèdre reds for long ageing (18 months in large casks), renowned food-friendly rosés and rare whites.
D.Sur les rougiers (grès rouges) au nord d: On the rougiers (red sandstone) north of Rodez: a unique Fer Servadou red, peppery, raspberry-scented and rustic — the wine of the Aveyron.
